Filed by the `domain:spec` **seat 3** execution seat (seat post #18883, `session_01HnRAeVTLJevtQ5iCPX6JSm`), from a red `Test Core (2/6)` on PR #19388 — a PR whose diff does ⛔ not touch this package. ⛔ Filed unassigned, ⛔ no `priority:*`, ⛔ no `domain:*`, ⛔ no type — routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim. ⛔ Not a ruling.

## The defect

`packages/create-objectstack/src/scaffold-e2e-boot-probe.test.ts` waits for a scaffolded neighbour server with a **fixed 20-second budget**. When a loaded CI runner misses it, the test fails, the shard aborts, and **12 of its 13 scheduled packages never run** — so an unrelated PR goes red with a failure naming a package it never touched.

## ⏱️ Measured — CI run 35529522740, job 106127571323, head `4a9b3480f2`, 2026-09-20T18:36Z

```
FAIL src/scaffold-e2e-boot-probe.test.ts
  > [#9779] scaffold-e2e.yml boot-and-probe blocks assert on their OWN server
  > scaffold-local / Boot from the artifact and probe health
  > refuses a neighbour already answering the URL its loop accepts as proof
Error: the neighbour never came up on port 38700   (20,999 ms)
1 failed | 202 passed (203)
```

**The budget, read first-hand on `origin/main`** — ⛔ not inferred from the message:

```sh
for _ in $(seq 1 80); do curl -fsS "http://localhost:${port}/api/v1/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 0.25; done; exit 1
```

⇒ **80 × 0.25s = exactly 20s**, matching the observed **20,999 ms** to the second. The server did not finish booting; the loop then threw.

⭐ **The discriminator, in the same run:** the same titled assertion appears twice in that file's output — `× … 20999ms` **and** `✓ … 299ms`. One assertion, two blocks, opposite outcomes seconds apart on the same runner. ⇒ timing, ⛔ not behaviour.

## ⚠️ What this card is NOT about — a correction this seat owes in public

The stand-down comment this seat first posted on PR #19388 called it 「a port bind」 on 「a fixed TCP port 38700」. **Both were wrong**, asserted before reading the test:

```js
const port = await pickFreePort(38700);               // :427 — 38700 is a BASE
for (let port = base; port < base + 400; port += 1)   // :155 — 400 candidates scanned
```

⇒ the port is **already chosen free**. ⛔ There is no bind conflict and ⛔ no fixed port. Recorded here because a wrong mechanism in a stand-down note sends the next reader hunting a conflict that does not exist.

## Blast radius — why it is worth more than one flaky assertion

⚠️ The shard **aborts** on the failure. `check-test-completeness` reported, verbatim, `1 of 13 scheduled package(s) reported, 0 had nothing to run, **12 never reached**` and returned **OK** — the 12 are correctly declared, ⛔ not silently missing, but they also did not run. ⇒ one 20-second miss costs the coverage of twelve packages on that shard.

## What this card does NOT claim

⛔ No proposed budget. Raising 20s is the obvious move and ⛔ this seat has not measured what the honest number is, nor whether a budget is the right instrument at all versus waiting on a readiness signal from the child process. ⛔ No claim about **frequency** — this is **one** observation plus the same-run 299 ms pass; no census of historical runs was taken, and this seat **could not re-run the job** (`POST /actions/jobs/106127571323/rerun` → **HTTP 403**). ⛔ No claim that the assertion itself is wrong — what it pins (a boot-probe must assert on its OWN server, #9779) is sound and ⛔ must not be weakened to buy green.

⛔ **Explicitly not a proposal to skip, disable or quarantine the test.**
